title: Work IQ: long-running tasks for A2A and MCP agents
summary: The roadmap facts, licensing statements and existing Work IQ controls are supported. The changed Microsoft pages do not invalidate the briefing; the spending-policy API row only needs its deciding request-body properties named in its note.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP mutation operations, including create, update, delete and sending email, are not allowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported Work IQ MCP mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio Work IQ experience documents write operations as on by default.
claims.quote: Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio write-operation default remains subject to organization permissions and policies.

claims.claim: A Work IQ request can fail with QuotaExhausted even when the tenant has prepaid credits.
claims.quote: A Work IQ chat request can fail with QuotaExhausted and the message "No AI credits are currently available for this user. Please request more credits from your admin." This error can happen even when the tenant has prepaid credits.

claims.claim: Spending policies define spending limits but do not reserve or allocate credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; controls[1].governs
claims.claim: A spending policy can include or exclude Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Excluding Work IQ API from one spending policy does not exclude it from other applicable policies.
claims.quote: Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: For users in a group spending policy, a running task that exceeds the per-user spending limit can complete without interruption.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.claim: That task's excess usage does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit, isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion), and doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards

claims.claim: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: Administrators can provision the service principal manually when it does not yet exist, for example before configuring MCP policy.
claims.quote: such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail. Tenant administrators can provision it

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy settings are reached in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an automation call for the Work IQ MCP tenant policy control.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com Work IQ MCP policy API update settings tenant policy Graph. Read policy governance, including Developer considerations; editable settings are discussed but no operation, endpoint or command is documented.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level on/off.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app and per-agent policy controls are not part of the initial Work IQ MCP policy surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: The documented MCP tenant policy control is not confirmed as an A2A or long-running-task-specific control.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The spending-policy creation workflow is opened at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy with credit limits and selected services.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies; Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note: "The request body sets periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings." These deciding properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-create.

claims.claim: The create spending-policy API requires CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: A spending policy created through this API is created disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.

claims.claim: The documented safe-create sequence links a group-scoped policy's audience using Add assigned group after creating the disabled policy.
claims.quote: For a group-scoped policy, follow the safe-create sequence: create the policy disabled, link its audience with Add assigned group, and let the service enable it once its requirements are satisfied.

claims.claim: Supplying nonempty assignedGroups during creation additionally requires CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Supplying a nonempty assignedGroups collection at creation additionally requires CopilotCostManagement-Assignment.ReadWrite.All.

claims.claim: The cited Cost Management Graph APIs use beta and are subject to change.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change.

claims.claim: Microsoft says use of these beta APIs in production applications is not supported.
claims.quote: Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The create spending-policy request requires @odata.type, displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: supply a JSON representation of a spendingPolicy object with a concrete @odata.type. Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Copilot Credit consumption reporting is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Consumption tab.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/serviceUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate} reports tenant credit consumption by service, including Work IQ.
claims.quote: GET /copilot/costManagement/usageReports/serviceUsageRecords?startDate={startDate}&endDate={endDate}; "@odata.context": "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/$metadata#Collection(microsoft.graph.costManagementServiceUsageRecord)"; "serviceId": "workIQ"

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Consumption tab has Policies and Agents and services views, and the latter reports Work IQ API consumption.
claims.quote: The Policies view is the default view when you open the Consumption tab. In the Agents and services view, review usage for supported services. For example, Cowork and Work IQ API.

claims.claim: The service usage records API reports exactly one completed UTC day per request.
claims.quote: The range must select exactly one completed UTC day. Current-day, future, and multi-day ranges are rejected, not clamped.

claims.claim: The service usage records API is general service-level consumption reporting rather than reporting specific to long-running tasks.
claims.quote: Get a list of costManagementServiceUsageRecord objects that report each governed service's share of the tenant's consumption of Copilot Credits for one completed UTC day.

claims.claim: az ad sp create --id fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 creates the Work IQ service principal in the organization.

claims.quote: This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.
